papers.title: Stability of graphene-based single-atom catalysts across the first-row transition series: the interplay of coordination, composition, and metal identity
papers.finding: DFT on 60 first-row TM SACs in mono/divacancy graphene, with and without N doping. Divacancies bind more strongly than monovacancies; C coordination beats N for the metal-graphene bond; stability is governed by d-state alignment with the graphene Fermi level; N doping weakens binding for late TMs.
papers.relation_note: Agrees with DV > SV (xTB variance result). It contradicts or complicates our N > S/C reading: it finds C beats N, while we find N holds better than S and see Co-N2OC as the only passing site. Closest systematic stability screen, but it uses hand-designed N-doped sites, not PDB enzyme sites.

papers.title: Reactivity screening of single atoms on modified graphene surface - from formation and scaling relations to catalytic activity
papers.finding: DFT on 9 metals (Ni, Cu, Ru, Rh, Pd, Ag, Ir, Pt, Au) on 4 supports. Only the single-vacancy graphene gives SACs stable against aggregation and dissolution under electrocatalysis conditions; only M@vacancy (not Ag, Au) is stable under HER in acid.
papers.relation_note: Finds SV sites stable against aggregation, while our E_f is positive for 18 of 20 sites. Likely a difference in definition (reference, pure C vacancy vs donor-substituted sites, metals studied). Needs reconciling with our E_f reference.

papers.title: Atomic adsorption on graphene with a single vacancy: systematic DFT study through the periodic table of elements
papers.finding: PBE/D2/D3/vdW-DF2 for elements of rows 1-6 at the SV. Binding correlates with the cohesive energy of the element. Dissolution potentials computed; most metals at the vacancy are more noble than in their bulk phase.
papers.relation_note: Same cohesive-energy correlation as our E_f trend. It is precedent for our U_diss approach, but limited to bare C3 vacancy without N/S/O donors.

papers.title: The Local Coordination Effects on the Reactivity and Speciation of Active Sites in Graphene-Embedded Single-Atom Catalysts over Wide pH and Potential Range
papers.finding: Mn, Fe, Co in M@N4 with N replaced by O or S (OxNy, SxNy). Replacing N with O or S destabilises the SACs towards dissolution (Pourbaix analysis).
papers.relation_note: Consistent with our N > S (and xTB: S and O hold the metal more weakly than N). Only 3 metals and DV N4 base; our work extends to 12 metals, C donors, and SV.

papers.title: Unraveling the Stability of N-Doped Graphene Supported Single-Atom and Dual-Atom Catalysts From Pourbaix Diagram
papers.finding: Pourbaix stability of Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni SACs/DACs on N-doped graphene. Co and Ni stable over wide pH/potential, Cr unstable everywhere; Fe and Mn stable only with adsorbates.
papers.relation_note: Method for pH-dependent U_diss with speciation and adsorbates; our U_diss is a simpler vacuum-style value. Co being most stable agrees with Co-N2OC being our only passing site.

papers.title: Activity And Stability of Single- And Di-Atom Catalysts for the O2 Reduction Reaction
papers.finding: Formation-energy plus Pourbaix screen of first-row TM SACs/DACs on defective N-graphene for ORR. MnNC found stable in acid and alkaline; 4 SACs and 15 DACs with high activity.
papers.relation_note: Template for coupling formation energy, stability and ORR activity; matches our ORR-intermediate aim. Handpicked N sites only, not enzyme-derived.

papers.title: The Nature and Stability of Transition Metal-Anchored Nitrogen-Doped Graphene Single-Atom Catalysts
papers.finding: Activation-strain and KS-MO analysis for Ti-Zn on the N4-doped support: metal-support interaction strengthens Ti to Ni and weakens Ni to Zn, due to filling of the 3dxy orbital.
papers.relation_note: Electronic explanation for the metal trend (Cu, Zn weakly bound) that we only see as correlation with cohesive energy; N4 only.

papers.title: Understanding stability and reactivity of transition metal single-atoms on graphene
papers.finding: PBE+D3 for Co, Ni, Rh, Pd, Ir, Pt on pristine graphene, hBN and monovacancy graphene. Monovacancy binds very strongly (up to 9.11 eV for Ir).
papers.relation_note: Adsorption energies on the bare vacancy are not formation energies vs bulk; limited metals and no donor variation.

papers.title: Mechanism of Particle-Mediated Inhibition of Demetalation for Single-Atom Catalytic Sites in Acidic Electrochemical Environments
papers.finding: Experimental: metal particles donate electrons to FeN4, strengthening Fe-N and cutting Fe dissolution by 78%; 430 h in a fuel cell.
papers.relation_note: Experimental demetalation context for the dissolution criterion; it is Fe-N4 only.

papers.title: Destabilization of Single-Atom Catalysts: Characterization, Mechanisms, and Regeneration Strategies
papers.finding: Review of SAC destabilization mechanisms, in situ characterization and regeneration (redispersion, poison desorption).
papers.relation_note: Context for the dissolution and aggregation failure modes we model; no screening data.

known: Metal-vacancy binding in graphene follows the metal cohesive energy, and divacancies bind more strongly than monovacancies. Local donor choice matters: replacing N with O or S destabilises dissolution stability, while C coordination binds the metal more strongly than N. Co and Ni are the most dissolution-stable among first-row metals in N-doped graphene, and Pourbaix analyses are the standard dissolution treatment. Studies are typically 5 to 60 hand-designed sites on 3 to 12 metals.
our_addition: Our screen is built from the coordination shells of PDB metalloenzyme sites and mixed N/S/O/C donors, reaching 1,138 xTB sites on 12 metals with DFT checks. Added on top are Arrhenius escape and NEB kinetics for pyrolysis conditions. Our positive E_f for 18 of 20 sites contrasts with the earlier report that the single vacancy is aggregation-stable (2101.02922), and we find N beats S (consistent with 36500932) but the Dalton paper finds C beats N.
gaps: From these abstracts, nobody has built a PDB-wide enzyme-to-SAC stability screen with real enzyme donor sets, nor compared enzyme donor sets against binding-maximising ones. The abstracts also show no kinetic escape barriers or pyrolysis-temperature criteria. Mixed N/S/O/C donors across many metals, and strain/geometry mismatch versus the enzyme site, are untreated here. The Pourbaix dissolution treatment is also not combined with a high-throughput screen across metals and donor sets. Only abstracts were read, so the novelty claim holds only against these 10 papers and the Dalton paper is the closest rival.

papers.title: Thermally Stable Single-Atom Heterogeneous Catalysts

papers.relation_note: Context for the pyrolysis-temperature criterion. It gives no quantitative barriers.

papers.title: Destabilization of Single-Atom Catalysts: Characterization, Mechanisms, and Regeneration Strategies
papers.finding: Review of SAC destabilization (active sites, coordination, support, conditions), in situ characterization, and regeneration by redispersion and other routes.
papers.relation_note: Background for the operating-stability side. It notes that structure-stability relationships are still lacking, which fits our gap.

papers.title: Trapping of metal atoms in vacancies of carbon nanotubes and graphene
papers.finding: In-situ STEM observed metal atoms trapped by graphene and nanotube vacancies, and escape from the traps studied over 20-670 C, which gives information on metal-defect bonding.
papers.relation_note: Experimental precedent for vacancy trapping and thermal escape on carbon. Its escape temperatures could serve as a rough check of our Arrhenius escape threshold (~3.5 eV at 800 C), and the abstract gives no numbers.

papers.title: Non defect-stabilized thermally stable single-atom catalyst
papers.finding: Pt single atoms stabilized by covalent metal-support interaction on reducible iron oxide, with no support defects involved. Stable through high-temperature calcination, with PtO2 vapor trapped.
papers.relation_note: Oxide-support, non-vacancy route. It does not bear on carbon-vacancy conclusions.

known: Single atoms migrate and agglomerate under pyrolysis and operating conditions. Graphene mono- and divacancy DFT studies show that divacancies bind metals more strongly than monovacancies and that stability follows metal identity and electronic alignment. Vacancy trapping and thermal escape have been observed directly by STEM on carbon (20-670 C). Adsorbates and operating conditions can lower migration barriers, and reviews already frame aggregation as a mix of thermodynamic and kinetic factors.
our_addition: We extend thermodynamics (E_f, U_diss) to enzyme-derived N/S/O/C donor sets across 12 metals and 1,138 xTB sites. We add NEB barriers close to the escape energy, which justifies a simple Arrhenius escape criterion at pyrolysis temperatures. Our finding that S and O bind more weakly than N is new next to the 2026 Dalton paper, which only compares N and C coordination. Our finding that only 1 of 20 sites is both thermodynamically and electrochemically stable also appears new.
gaps: None of the abstracts shows a PDB-wide or enzyme-derived stability screen, S/O donor sets in graphene vacancies, or escape barriers tied to a pyrolysis-temperature criterion across many metals. None reports ML-potential or AIMD aggregation on carbon vacancies, and the two sintering/ML candidates (Pt on silica, multiscale Pt sintering) were not opened. Operation-induced effects such as adsorbate-assisted escape are not included in our work. The 2010 STEM escape data could not be compared quantitatively from the abstract alone.

papers.relation_note: Broad reference for control and verification of mixed shells.

papers.title: The Nature and Stability of Transition Metal-Anchored Nitrogen-Doped Graphene Single-Atom Catalysts
papers.finding: Energy decomposition analysis for Ti to Zn on a four-N-doped graphene support. Metal-support binding strengthens from Ti to Ni and weakens from Ni to Zn, explained by the filling of the 3dxy orbital.
papers.relation_note: Gives a non-monotonic metal trend for N4 sites. Compare with our finding that E_f follows bulk cohesive energy, which is a different descriptor that may be partly consistent. It covers N4 only.

known: Mixed N/S, N/O and N/C first shells on carbon (Fe-N3S, Co-N3S, Ni-N2O2) are made experimentally, by co-doping or by molecular and coordination-compound precursors. They are checked with EXAFS and XANES (and Mossbauer, operando XAS), which can separate first-shell S from second-shell S. Computational stability screens of graphene SACs show that divacancies bind better than monovacancies, that C and N donors differ, and that the metal trend is non-monotonic and tied to d-state alignment. Systematic data on S/O donor stability against clustering, and on operando stability of S/O sites, are thin in these abstracts.
our_addition: Our PDB-derived screen adds a broad, enzyme-based set of N/S/O/C donor sets, vacancy types and 12 metals. Three results are new relative to these abstracts. Most sites have E_f > 0, with only Co-N2OC (DV) stable. S and O hold the metal more weakly than N and C. A kinetic escape-barrier criterion links pyrolysis temperature to survival. The DV > SV result agrees with the literature, but the N-versus-C ordering needs to be checked against d6dt01022a, which finds C better than N.
gaps: As far as these abstracts show, no one has used the enzyme first coordination shells as a systematic source of SAC sites. No one has combined thermodynamic E_f with escape and NEB barriers and an Arrhenius pyrolysis criterion for mixed N/S/O/C shells. No one has compared enzyme geometry with the rigid vacancy geometry (shorter bonds, out-of-plane metal). Experimental work reports activity for individual Fe/Co-N3S and Ni-N2O2 sites but gives no systematic stability comparison of S and O sites against N. Whether Co-N2OC has been made is not addressed. Note that abstracts only: the stability results of 10.1039/d2nr04880a and the donor scope of 10.1039/d6cp00932h need full-text checks.

papers.title: Natural biomass derived single-atom catalysts for energy and environmental applications
papers.finding: Review: over forty SAC types made from starch, cellulose, lignin, proteins, chitin, with Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn, Mn, Pt, for ORR, OER, HER.
papers.relation_note: Covers the pyrolysis synthesis context for our 800-1000 C escape criterion; no stability criterion.

known: Bioinspired SAC design is established as a qualitative principle (first-shell and second-shell mimicry of hydrogenase, nitrogenase, oxidase), and several experimental routes make enzyme-like M-N/O/S sites from proteins, metalloprotein-MOFs or biomass by pyrolysis (FeN5-xOx, FeN3S, Zn-N4 geometries). Coordination tuning (axial S, geometry, N/O/S mix) is shown to change nanozyme activity. Reviews state that SAC stability is limited and that stability design is still largely empirical. High-throughput use of the PDB exists for enzyme cluster models (QuantumPDB, 989 holo-enzymes).
our_addition: We add a PDB-wide transfer of metalloenzyme first shells into graphene vacancies with computed thermodynamic (E_f, U_diss) and kinetic (escape energy, NEB) stability, showing most sites (18 of 20 by DFT) are unstable against clustering and only Co-N2OC passes. This quantifies an N > S/O stability penalty that the activity-focused S- and O-doped experimental papers do not address, and shows the rigid support distorts enzyme geometry.
gaps: As far as these abstracts show, none combines PDB-wide first-shell extraction with SAC construction and a computed stability screen (E_f, dissolution potential, escape barrier). Bioinspired SAC work is experimental or single-system, stability is treated qualitatively, and QuantumPDB stops at enzyme cluster models. Also absent: an explicit check of enzyme-site geometry retention on a graphene support, and an activity-versus-stability trade-off for S/O donor sets. Caveat: only a title search and ten abstracts were checked, so the novelty claim is not proven by absence.

papers.relation_note: Experimental evidence that support-imposed geometry changes activity; supports our point that the rigid flat graphene differs from the enzyme geometry in a way that matters.

papers.title: Generalizable mechanochemical impact of curvature governing stability and reactivity at catalytic sites on rippled supports
papers.finding: DFT on 3d/4d/5d M-N-C sites: curvature changes thermodynamic stability (larger metals favoured at higher curvature), H binding and CO2 activation, strongest for early metals.
papers.relation_note: Directly bears on our finding that strain adds nothing in xTB and on dG_H; they find a curvature effect on stability, so our flat-support strain null result may not carry over to curved supports.

papers.title: Effect of Strain Engineering on the Spin State of the Ni-N4/C Single-Atom Catalyst and Its Consequence in Electrocatalysis
papers.finding: Tensile strain on Ni-N4/C switches Ni from low to high spin and improves O2 and CO2 electroreduction activity.
papers.relation_note: Strain affects activity via spin state, which our closed-shell-style stability screen and dG_H do not capture.

papers.title: Substrate Strain Engineering of Single-Atomic Sn-N4 Sites Embedded in Various Carbon Matrixes for Bifunctional Oxygen Electrocatalysis
papers.finding: Sn-N4 forms a pyramid; strain transfer to CNT, GQD and graphene supports changes O-intermediate binding and breaks scaling relations in CNTs.
papers.relation_note: Large metal out of plane plus support strain affects ORR intermediates; relevant to our out-of-plane displacement and the ORR intermediates being computed.

papers.title: Unveiling the critical role of strain-induced local structure changes in Co-N4 single-atom catalysts for enhanced oxygen reduction and evolution reactions
papers.finding: DFT: directional strain tuning M-N distances optimizes ORR/OER with OOH* formation as common rate-determining step; coordination type (pyridinic vs pyrrolic) dominates.
papers.relation_note: Supports our observation that M-donor bond lengths (shortened by 0.1-0.4 A on graphene) matter for activity; Co is also our one stable site.

papers.title: Potential-Induced Dynamic Coordination of Nonmetal Atoms Directly Bound to Metal Centers in Graphene-Embedded Single-Atom Catalysts and Its Implications
papers.finding: Constant-potential DFT/AIMD on NiN4-xCx: C donors bound to Ni hydrogenate under potential, N donors do not; this reshapes the site and weakens adsorption.
papers.relation_note: Suggests our C-donor sites (e.g. Co-N2OC) may not remain intact under operating potential, a caveat to the U_diss stability claim; N donors are robust.

known: Divacancies bind single atoms more strongly than monovacancies, the metal-support bond follows d-state alignment and metal identity, and N donors raise migration barriers for Fe. Support curvature and strain change site geometry, metal-donor distances, spin state, and ORR/CO2 activity, and an out-of-plane metal (Fe-N3, Sn-N4) gives reactivity that electronic structure alone does not predict. Systematic stability screens exist for first-row metals in generic N/C vacancy sites.
our_addition: We start from the actual first coordination shells of PDB metalloenzymes (N, S, O, C donors), cover 12 metals and 1,138 sites, and combine DFT E_f, U_diss, escape energy and NEB kinetics. We find that S/O hold weaker than N, that enzyme donor sets do not maximise binding, and that only Co-N2OC is stable. The rigid-support geometry mismatch versus enzyme and molecular complexes is quantified (about 2/3 from the support).
gaps: Within these abstracts, no study derives SAC sites from enzyme active sites PDB-wide, so the novelty claim stands (the closest is 42695769, a 60-SAC generic screen). No abstract compares graphene-embedded geometries against the enzyme or molecular porphyrin/phthalocyanine complexes with a decomposition of support-induced change. Curvature and strain effects on stability (41924911) were not tested with S/O donors or kinetic barriers. Phthalocyanine out-of-plane and degradation papers were not opened, and none of the abstracts covers S/O-donor sites under potential.

papers.title: Stability of graphene-based single-atom catalysts across the first-row transition series: the interplay of coordination, composition, and metal identity
papers.finding: DFT study of 60 3d-metal SACs on mono- and divacancy graphene, with and without N doping. Divacancies bind more strongly than monovacancies. C coordination beats N coordination for the metal-graphene bond. Stability follows alignment of metal d states with the graphene Fermi level. For late metals, N doping weakens binding.
papers.relation_note: Agrees with our DV > SV result and with metal-identity trends. Its C > N finding sits close to our xTB result that C holds metal well. Our N > S ordering is not tested here because it has no S or O donors. Closest published systematic SV/DV stability study, but only 3d metals, no enzyme-derived sites.

papers.title: Unraveling the Stability of N-Doped Graphene Supported Single-Atom and Dual-Atom Catalysts From Pourbaix Diagram
papers.finding: Pourbaix-based electrochemical stability of Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni SACs and DACs on N-doped graphene, including leached-metal speciation and H-capped vacancies. Co- and Ni-SAC are stable over wide pH and potential ranges. Cr-SAC is unstable everywhere, and DAC stable regions are smaller than SAC ones.
papers.relation_note: Goes beyond our U_diss: it adds pH, adsorbate effects and vacancy H-capping. Co being the most stable agrees with our Co-N2OC (U_diss +0.51 V). Shows our dissolution potential is only a first-order criterion.

papers.title: Fast-Track to Catalyst Stability: Machine Learning Optimized Predictions for M1/M2-N6-Gra Catalysts
papers.finding: MLP trained on 143 DFT samples predicts formation energies of 1134 dual-atom M1/M2-N6-Gra catalysts (test R2 0.98). 604 have E_f < 0. Coordination number controls E_f. Cohesive energy dominates at low coordination, and metal-substrate binding at high coordination.
papers.relation_note: Supports our finding that E_f follows bulk cohesive energy. Supplies a feature set and transfer-learning recipe we could use on our xTB library. Only N6 dual-metal sites.

papers.title: LOCAL: A Locality-based Active Learning Framework for Predicting the Stability of Dual-Atom Catalysts
papers.finding: GCN plus active learning predicts stability of dual-atom catalysts on N-doped graphene over 611,648 structures. Test MAE is 0.15 eV with DFT on only 2.7 % of the data. COHP-based locality is used and phase diagrams are validated against synthesized configurations.
papers.relation_note: Template for scaling our 1,138-site xTB set with active learning, using xTB or DFT labels. N-only donors, no S, O or enzyme-derived sites.

papers.title: Transfer learning with domain knowledge adaptation for stability evaluation of dual-atom catalysts on nitrogen-doped carbon
papers.finding: Transfer learning evaluates stability against metal aggregation for dual-atom catalysts on N-doped carbon. Stability descriptors learned on single atoms on doped carbon transfer to dual-atom sites.
papers.relation_note: Aggregation-based stability is the same notion as our E_f vs bulk. Suggests the descriptors from our xTB set could transfer to the DFT subset. The abstract gives no numbers.

papers.title: Active learning accelerated exploration of single-atom local environments in multimetallic systems for oxygen electrocatalysis
papers.finding: Equivariant GNN surrogate with active learning explores more than 30,000 binary 3d-metal single-atom sites with varying ligand environments for ORR/OER. The targets are DFT binding energies and descriptors, not stability. Co-Fe, Co-Co and Co-Zn pairs are predicted promising.
papers.relation_note: Shows that ML over many metals and coordinations is established for activity. It does not address stability or synthesizability, which leaves our focus open.

papers.title: An Atlas and Design Rules for Single- and Dual-Atom Alloys
papers.finding: DFT atlas of transition-metal single- and dual-atom alloys in Cu and Ag surfaces, validated by STM. Stability follows an electron count (pairing is strongest near d10), with size mismatch and spin as modifiers.
papers.relation_note: Atlas-style systematic stability work, but for alloy surfaces, not carbon-supported SACs. Parallels our metal-trend analysis (d-filling, cohesion).

papers.title: Single-Atom Saturation: A Fundamental Principle for Single-Atom-Site Catalyst Design
papers.finding: Proposes a descriptor combining d-electron saturation and coordination saturation of the single atom to predict intermediate binding on single-atom alloys. It also applies to N-doped graphene SACs. It targets activity, not stability.
papers.relation_note: Coordination and d-occupancy descriptors are candidates for explaining our donor-set results. It is an activity descriptor, so it says nothing directly about stability or synthesis.

papers.title: New Frontiers in Single-Atom Catalysis: Active-Site Dynamics and AI-Enabled Design
papers.finding: Review of active-site evolution in SACs (atomic migration, coordination changes) and of in situ characterization, multiscale modeling and ML as routes to design.
papers.relation_note: Frames our escape-energy and NEB kinetics as part of site dynamics. Good citation for introduction and outlook.

known: ML and active learning for SAC and DAC stability are established, but only on N-coordinated dual-atom or N6 graphene sites: MLP formation-energy models (1134 sites), GCN active learning (611,648 structures, MAE 0.15 eV), and transfer of aggregation-stability descriptors. Systematic DFT on graphene SACs shows that divacancies bind more strongly than monovacancies, and that stability follows metal d-state alignment and cohesive energy. Electrochemical (Pourbaix) work finds Co and Ni SACs the most robust and DACs less stable than SACs. ML across many metals and coordinations exists for activity (30,000+ sites), not for stability.
our_addition: We add stability and kinetic data (E_f, U_diss, escape energy, NEB barriers with an Arrhenius pyrolysis criterion) for sites whose donor sets come from PDB metalloenzymes, with N, S, O and C donors. We also show that enzyme donor sets do not maximise binding. Our C-versus-N and DV-versus-SV trends are consistent with the Dalton 2026 paper, and the cohesive-energy dependence with Fast-Track.
gaps: None of the abstracts shows a PDB-wide or enzyme-derived screen, or S/O donors in graphene vacancies. None combines thermodynamic stability with kinetic barriers against escape, or an Arrhenius synthesis-temperature criterion. ML work covers only N-coordinated (dual-atom) sites. No ML or active-learning model for stability across mixed N/S/O/C donor sets and many metals was found, so our xTB library of 1,138 sites could be that dataset. Caveat: these are title and abstract searches, so the novelty claim rests on the abstracts only.
